title: Tanto es así que: reforzar una afirmación

sections.content: Tanto es así que (so much so that) reinforces a claim by pointing to concrete proof of just how true it was -- ideal for a reading that wants to show, not just tell, how powerful Perón's and Evita's popular support really was. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Perón impulsó mejoras salariales y una expansión de los derechos sindicales; tanto es así que, cuando intentaron apartarlo del poder, decenas de miles de trabajadores se movilizaron para exigir su liberación.
items.english: Perón pushed for wage improvements and an expansion of union rights; so much so that, when they tried to remove him from power, tens of thousands of workers mobilized to demand his release.

items.spanish: Eva Duarte se convirtió en una figura de enorme influencia; tanto es así que, tras su muerte prematura, el país entero entró en un duelo verdaderamente masivo.
items.english: Eva Duarte became a figure of enormous influence; so much so that, after her early death, the entire country entered into truly massive mourning.

items.spanish: El gobierno combinó redistribución con métodos autoritarios; tanto es así que los historiadores siguen debatiendo cómo entender el peronismo.
items.english: The government combined redistribution with authoritarian methods; so much so that historians still debate how to understand Peronism.

items.spanish: Aquel episodio se convirtió en la fecha fundacional del movimiento peronista, y Perón ganó las elecciones apenas unos meses después.
items.english: That episode became the founding date of the Peronist movement, and Perón won the elections just a few months later.

sections.content: Tanto es así que always follows the claim it's reinforcing, usually after a semicolon or period -- it never opens a paragraph on its own, since it needs something concrete to point back to.
